questions.q: What makes the ideal product manager, according to Cagan?
a: Technical depth plus strong social and networking skills
Years of seniority inside the same company
A marketing degree and sales experience
An ability to code every part of the product
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the ideal lead is bilingual, with a strong technical base and people skills.

questions.q: Which roles does a strong product team include besides the product manager?
a: A user experience designer and a marketing person
A lawyer and a financial controller
A data scientist and a customer support lead
An investor and a board advisor
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists a UX designer and a marketing person as the product manager's closest partners.

questions.q: What do interaction designers do in the product process?
a: They map what users want into a blueprint for the product
They build the visual interface from finished designs
They test prototypes like an ordinary consumer
They pitch the finished product to investors
questions.why: Lesson 2 says interaction designers understand user needs, then create the blueprint others build on.

questions.q: What is the only purpose of a prototype?
a: To mimic the experience and reveal mistakes early
To serve as the final version sent to customers
To show investors how much has been spent
To replace testing with a polished demo
questions.why: Lesson 2 says prototypes exist to imitate the product and help the team spot errors before building.

questions.q: What three traits must a successful product have?
a: Feasible, usable and valuable
Fast, cheap and original
Novel, complex and expensive
Popular, stylish and simple
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the product must be buildable, usable by customers and worth buying.
